mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous 3 months signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator for economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increases by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the previous 3 months signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the previous 6 months signals robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS shows a sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds the historical average by more than 1%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds the historical average by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the previous 3 months signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase & UNRATE decrease in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the previous 3 months signals a robust economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase & UNRATE decrease in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 increases and UNRATE decreases.
